title: Speaks the Nightbird
author: McCammon, Robert
review:
A colonial mystery horror whodunnit witch trial with Sherlock Holmes vibes, what's not to like?

McCammon has written another masterpiece here, the atmosphere and environment that he builds here is nothing short of extraordinary, it really feels like you're in the age of the frontier colonial America; superstition is high and knowledge / trust in science is low and the horror of the ignorance of humanity is in full force as they see the Devil in every shadow and misread signs from God in day to day life.

The character work here is exceptional as well, Corbett is a great character and you get a lot of backstory from him, his mentor, and other characters as well in a way that's natural during the narrative.

The themes McCammon explores are very interesting and poignant, he uses his prose to delve beneath the surface of a great plot to elevate the narrative and ask the big questions of good vs evil and the folly of man. It's interesting what has changed and also frightening what has stayed the same, the horror found in the souls of our fellow humans can be scarier than the demons in the darkest of corners of the colonial swamps.

I pretty much devoured this and the mysteries are very interesting and come together in a perfect way that is nothing short of genius, the way McCammon plots out his books works so well for me.

Had to restrain myself from starting book 2 immediately. I can't wait to see what Mr Corbett will be up to next.
